statements.value: A nitrogen oxoanion formed by loss of a proton from nitric acid. Principal species present at pH 7.3.
The nitrogen oxoanion formed by loss of a proton from nitrous acid.
A nitrogen oxide which is a free radical, each molecule of which consists of one nitrogen and one oxygen atom.

A nitrogen oxide consisting of linear unsymmetrical molecules with formula N<small><sub>2</sub></small>O. While it is the most used gaseous anaesthetic in the world, its major commercial use, due to its solubility under pressure in vegetable fats combined with its non-toxicity in low concentrations, is as an aerosol spray propellant and aerating agent for canisters of 'whipped' cream.
An elemental molecule consisting of two trivalently-bonded nitrogen atoms.
An oxygen hydride consisting of an oxygen atom that is covalently bonded to two hydrogen atoms

The general name for the hydrogen nucleus, to be used without regard to the hydrogen nuclear mass (either for hydrogen in its natural abundance or where it is not desired to distinguish between the isotopes).
An organophosphate oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the diphosphate OH groups of molybdate-bis(molybdopterin guanine dinucleotide); major species at pH 7.3.
An Fe<small><sub>4</sub></small>S<small><sub>4</sub></small> iron-sulfur cluster in which each sulfur is attached to three of the iron atoms.
The cyclic tetrapyrrole anion that is ferroheme c protonated to pH 7.3.
A cyclic tetrapyrrole anion arising from deprotonation of the four carboxy groups of ferroheme d1; major species at pH 7.3.
Dicarboxylate anion of ferroheme b; major species at pH 7.3.
An inorganic group consisting of two copper atoms in close proximity (charge not specified).
The contents of a cell excluding the plasma membrane and nucleus, but including other subcellular structures.
The region between the inner (cytoplasmic) and outer membrane (Gram-negative Bacteria) or cytoplasmic membrane and cell wall (Fungi and Gram-positive Bacteria).
The membrane surrounding a cell that separates the cell from its external environment. It consists of a phospholipid bilayer and associated proteins.
The reduction of nitrate to dinitrogen by four reduction reactions: nitrate reduced to nitrite, then to nitric oxide, then to nitrous oxide, and finally to dinitrogen.
A lipid bilayer along with all the proteins and protein complexes embedded in it and attached to it.
